goals.name: 35% reduction of fecal coliform loads per 2002 TMDL
goals.description: The plan adopts the 2002 TMDL's 35% fecal coliform load reduction as the target its management strategies are meant to meet or exceed.
goals.targetText: meet and/or exceed the goal of a 35% reduction as put forth by the 2002 TMDL
goals.sourceQuote: Where applicable, expected reductions to fecal coliform loads are indicated to demonstrate ability to meet and/or exceed the goal of a 35% reduction as put forth by the 2002 TMDL.

goals.name: Reduce nutrient loads and sediments from nonpoint sources
goals.description: Beyond the bacteria TMDL, the plan recommends measures to reduce nutrient and sediment loads entering the watershed from nonpoint sources.
goals.targetText: reduce nutrient loads and sediments coming from nonpoint sources
goals.sourceQuote: As such, this WIP also recommends taking measures to reduce nutrient loads and sediments coming from nonpoint sources in the watershed.

goals.name: Vision: a cleaner watershed for healthier humans and ecosystems
goals.description: The community vision calls for a cleaner watershed, public access to the bayou and recreation, and an educated, engaged stakeholder base.
goals.targetText: a cleaner watershed for healthier humans and ecosystems
goals.sourceQuote: The community envisions a cleaner watershed for healthier humans and ecosystems; where residents and visitors have access to the bayou and wholesome recreational opportunities; and where stakeholders are educated and actively engaged in protecting the watershed.

goals.name: Better understand and reduce pollutants entering the water system
goals.description: The first plan goal is to improve understanding of pollutant sources and to reduce the pollutants reaching Old Fort Bayou.
goals.targetText: reduce pollutants entering the water system
goals.sourceQuote: Better understand and reduce pollutants entering the water system

goals.name: Update and continue water quality monitoring, add TN and TP
goals.description: Objective to update ongoing water quality monitoring in the watershed and add Total Nitrogen and Total Phosphorus as indicators.
goals.sourceQuote: Update and continue to monitor water quality in Old Fort Bayou Watershed and add indicators including, but not limited to Total Nitrogen and Total Phosphorus

goals.name: Identify contributors of pathogens and reduce harmful bacteria
goals.description: Objective to identify specific pathogen sources and target them to reduce bacteria entering the water.
goals.targetText: reduce harmful bacteria entering the water system
goals.sourceQuote: Identify specific contributors of pathogens and target to reduce harmful bacteria entering the water system

goals.name: Promote and enforce litter prevention
goals.description: Objective to reduce litter entering the watershed through promotion and enforcement of litter prevention.

goals.name: Reduce erosion and sedimentation to improve water quality
goals.description: The second goal is to reduce erosion and sedimentation, improving water quality and protecting navigability of Old Fort Bayou.
goals.targetText: improve water quality and protect navigability of Old Fort Bayou
goals.sourceQuote: Reduce erosion and sedimentation to improve water quality and protect navigability of Old Fort Bayou

goals.name: Identify and target key sources of erosion
goals.description: Objective to locate the main erosion sources in the watershed and focus actions on them.
goals.sourceQuote: Identify and target key sources of erosion

goals.name: Promote Low Impact Development and reduce stormwater runoff
goals.description: Objective to encourage policies and practices that promote Low Impact Development and reduce stormwater runoff.
goals.targetText: reduce stormwater runoff in the watershed
goals.sourceQuote: Encourage policies and practices to promote the use of Low Impact Development strategies and reduce stormwater runoff in the watershed

goals.name: Protect and re-establish riparian buffers
goals.description: Objective to protect existing riparian buffers and re-establish them where possible.
goals.sourceQuote: Protect and re-establish riparian buffers where possible

goals.name: Protect and improve access points and recreational opportunities
goals.description: The third goal is to protect and improve quality access points and recreation on and around Old Fort Bayou.
goals.sourceQuote: Protect and improve quality access points and recreational opportunities on and around Old Fort Bayou

goals.name: Re-assess, update and promote Old Fort Bayou blueway
goals.description: Objective to re-assess, update and promote the blueway and its supporting infrastructure.
goals.sourceQuote: Re-assess, update and promote Old Fort Bayou blueway and supporting infrastructure

goals.name: Coordinate planning of future public access points
goals.description: Objective to coordinate planning and development of future public access points in line with current BMPs.
goals.sourceQuote: Coordinate planning and development of future public access points, keeping in line with current Best Management Practices

goals.name: Support environmentally-sensitive recreation and economic development
goals.description: Objective to support recreation and economic development that preserves marshes and riparian buffers.
goals.sourceQuote: Support environmentally-sensitive recreation and economic development opportunities that allow for preservation of marshes and riparian buffers

goals.name: Increase environmental awareness, stewardship and participation
goals.description: The fourth goal is to raise environmental awareness and stewardship and increase stakeholder participation in the watershed.
goals.sourceQuote: Increase environmental awareness, stewardship and stakeholder participation in the watershed

goals.name: Establish an Old Fort Bayou Watershed Partnership
goals.description: Objective to keep the Steering and Technical Advisory Committee active and form a formal watershed partnership.
goals.sourceQuote: Build momentum of the Steering and Technical Advisory Committee for the Old Fort Bayou WIP and establish an Old Fort Bayou Watershed Partnership

goals.name: Implement and improve education and outreach plan
goals.description: Objective to carry out and continue to improve the watershed education and outreach plan.
goals.sourceQuote: Implement and continue to improve plan for education and outreach in the watershed

goals.name: Create opportunities for monitoring and stewardship participation
goals.description: Objective to give schools, civic organizations and residents meaningful ways to take part in water quality monitoring and stewardship.
goals.sourceQuote: Create meaningful opportunities for schools, civic organizations and residents to participate in water quality monitoring and stewardship activities

bmps.name: Conservation & Restoration at Bayou Talla (land acquisition)
bmps.description: LTMCP is negotiating acquisition of 13.98 acres along Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla. The aim is to preserve riparian buffers in critical areas.
bmps.location: Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla
bmps.sourceQuote: The Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain is currently negotiating acquisition of several properties totaling 13.98 acres along Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla.

bmps.name: Conservation and Riparian Buffers (property/easement acquisition)
bmps.description: LTMCP is to keep working with local governments and landowners to acquire property or easements. The focus is on preserving, expanding and restoring riparian buffers along Old Fort Bayou.
bmps.location: Old Fort Bayou
bmps.sourceQuote: LTMCP should continue to work with Jackson County, Ocean Springs, Gautier and private landowners within the watershed to acquire property or easements that will protect critical land within the watershed.

bmps.name: Living Shorelines and Marsh Restoration
bmps.description: Removing derelict structures and hardened shorelines along Old Fort Bayou and replacing them with living shorelines to reduce erosion.
bmps.location: Old Fort Bayou
bmps.sourceQuote: there are also quite a few opportunities to remove derelict structures and hardened shorelines and replace them with living shorelines.

bmps.name: Trash Catches in Commercial Area
bmps.description: Installing trash catches or drain guards at catch basins in curb-and-gutter commercial areas so litter does not reach waterways.
bmps.location: commercial areas
bmps.sourceQuote: Trash catches or drain guards installed at the catch basins would help prevent litter from entering the waterways.

bmps.name: Street sweeping
bmps.description: Regular street sweeping, coordinated by county and city road maintenance departments, to keep roadway litter and debris out of the drainage system.
bmps.sourceQuote: Regular street sweeping should be coordinated through the county and city road maintenance departments.

bmps.name: Stormwater Ordinance Updates
bmps.description: Assessing and improving the jurisdictions' stormwater-related ordinances. The Jackson County assessment is to be done through the B-WET program.
bmps.location: Jackson County
bmps.sourceQuote: This assessment is to be completed for Jackson County as part of the B-WET program underway with St. Martin High School as described above and in Appendix E.

bmps.name: Coastal Technical Manual (coastal stormwater supplement)
bmps.description: MDEQ to add a coastal supplement to its stormwater technical manual, or adopt Georgia's Coastal Stormwater Supplement, to guide stormwater BMPs on the coast.
bmps.sourceQuote: MDEQ should consider adding a coastal supplement to their technical manual so it is more relevant to jurisdictions on the coast or adopting Georgia’s Coastal Stormwater Supplement to the Georgia Stormwater Management Manual.

bmps.name: Fertilizer Ordinance
bmps.description: Jurisdictions to consider adopting a fertilizer ordinance, paired with outreach, to cut urban nutrient loading to Old Fort Bayou.
bmps.location: Old Fort Bayou Watershed urban areas
bmps.sourceQuote: The jurisdictions in Old Fort Bayou Watershed should consider adopting some form of fertilizer ordinance, in coordination with education and outreach to property owners and lawn care businesses about responsible fertilizer use, as a means of reducing nutrients entering Old Fort Bayou.

bmps.name: Pre and Post Construction SWPPP enforcement
bmps.description: MDEQ and the jurisdictions to increase their capacity to monitor and enforce construction Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans so erosion is controlled.
bmps.sourceQuote: MDEQ and the jurisdictions need to view erosion and stormwater control as a priority and increase their capacity to monitor and enforce SWPPP’s.

bmps.name: Drainage swale maintenance
bmps.description: Proper maintenance of the watershed's open grassy drainage swales: litter control, keeping vegetative cover, removing sediment and revegetating.
bmps.sourceQuote: In order to function at an optimal level, however, swales need to be properly maintained.

bmps.name: Small Scale Urban BMPs (rain barrels and rain gardens)
bmps.description: Encouraging rain barrels and rain gardens in developed areas, including highly visible demonstration projects at local businesses and organizations.
bmps.location: developed areas of the watershed
bmps.sourceQuote: Rain barrels and rain gardens are examples of smaller scale urban BMPs that can have a significant positive impact on water quality if implemented throughout a community.

bmps.name: Logging BMPs incentive/ordinance
bmps.description: Jackson County to consider a cost-share or timber harvest ordinance mechanism to increase use of forestry and logging BMPs.
bmps.location: Jackson County
bmps.sourceQuote: Jackson County should consider using a similar mechanism to increase the implementation of logging BMPs.

bmps.name: Nonfunctioning septic system assessment and maintenance program
bmps.description: Updated assessment of remaining nonfunctioning septic systems, combined with a campaign on proper maintenance, to address pathogen sources.
bmps.location: northern tip and south-central areas of the watershed
bmps.sourceQuote: An updated assessment of remaining nonfunctioning septic systems should be conducted, coupled with an educational campaign about the risks of nonfunctioning septic systems and proper maintenance.

bmps.name: Pet waste signage and receptacles
bmps.description: Providing pet waste receptacles and signage where people frequently walk pets, to reduce bacteria from pet waste.
bmps.sourceQuote: Signage and waste receptacles should also be provided in areas where people frequently walk pets.

bmps.name: Golf course BMPs at Gulf Hills
bmps.description: Opportunity to implement water quality BMPs, with outreach, at Gulf Hills Golf Course, which drains into Old Fort Bayou.
bmps.location: Gulf Hills Golf Course
bmps.sourceQuote: there is a significant opportunity for implementing BMPs coupled with outreach and education.

bmps.name: Vegetative buffer strips (The Preserve Golf Club)
bmps.description: Existing vegetative buffer strips at The Preserve Golf Club adjacent to Old Fort Bayou.
bmps.location: The Preserve Golf Club
bmps.sourceQuote: Vegetative buffer strips

bmps.name: Mitigated wetlands (The Preserve Golf Club)
bmps.description: About 32 acres of mitigated wetlands at The Preserve Golf Club, a certified Audubon Signature Sanctuary.
bmps.location: The Preserve Golf Club
bmps.sourceQuote: In addition to being home to approximately 32 acres of mitigated wetlands, The Preserve is a showcase of many Best Management Practices.

bmps.name: Irrigation system to minimize drift (The Preserve Golf Club)
bmps.description: Existing irrigation system at The Preserve designed to minimize drift and maximize water use efficiency.
bmps.location: The Preserve Golf Club
bmps.sourceQuote: Irrigation system to minimize drift and maximize water use efficiency

bmps.name: Special management zones (The Preserve Golf Club)
bmps.description: No-spray or limited-spray zones at The Preserve Golf Club.
bmps.location: The Preserve Golf Club
bmps.sourceQuote: Special management zones (i.e. no or limited spray)

bmps.name: Proper storage of fertilizers and pesticides (The Preserve Golf Club)
bmps.description: Existing practice at The Preserve of storing fertilizers and pesticides properly to prevent contamination.
bmps.location: The Preserve Golf Club
bmps.sourceQuote: Proper storage of fertilizers and pesticides

bmps.name: Erosion control of roads and trails (TNC Old Fort Bayou Mitigation Bank)
bmps.description: Erosion control on roads and trails, carried out by The Nature Conservancy on its Old Fort Bayou Mitigation Bank.
bmps.location: TNC Old Fort Bayou Mitigation Bank
bmps.sourceQuote: Erosion control of roads and trails

implementation.name: First watershed assessment and plan revision in 2023
implementation.description: The plan calls for routine integrated assessments of the watershed and amendments to the WIP based on their results. The first assessment and revision is scheduled for 2023, five years after the 2018 assessment.
implementation.responsibleParty: Old Fort Bayou Watershed Partnership
implementation.sourceQuote: The Old Fort Bayou Watershed Partnership should begin conducting its first assessment and plan revision in 2023.

implementation.name: Jackson County Stormwater Task Force to adopt responsibility for the WIP
implementation.description: No formal watershed partnership exists yet. The plan recommends that the existing Jackson County Stormwater Task Force take over the WIP, adding members from the Steering and Technical Advisory Committee.
implementation.responsibleParty: Jackson County Stormwater Task Force
implementation.sourceQuote: Since this task force already deals with many overlapping areas including stormwater management BMPs and outreach and education, it would be an easy transition for this group to adopt responsibility for the Old Fort Bayou Watershed Implementation Plan.

implementation.name: MDEQ to consider funding a watershed coordinator grant program
implementation.description: As an alternative way to sustain leadership for the plan, MDEQ could fund a watershed coordinator grant program modelled on California's.
implementation.responsibleParty: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality
implementation.sourceQuote: Another option would be for The Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality to consider funding a watershed coordinator grant program similar to what was done in California through the Department of Conservation.

implementation.name: MDEQ enlisted LTMCP and GCCDS to facilitate WIP development
implementation.description: Project management step: in May 2018 MDEQ engaged the Land Trust and MSU's Gulf Coast Community Design Studio to facilitate development of the Watershed Implementation Plan.
implementation.responsibleParty: MDEQ; Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain; Gulf Coast Community Design Studio
implementation.sourceQuote: In May 2018, MDEQ enlisted the Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain (LTMCP), in partnership with Mississippi State University’s Gulf Coast Community Design Studio, to facilitate the development of a Watershed Implementation Plan for Old Fort Bayou Watershed.

implementation.name: Assemble Watershed Implementation Team
implementation.description: The first step of the planning process was forming a Watershed Implementation Team representing watershed stakeholders. It includes a Steering and Technical Advisory Committee and an Education and Outreach Subcommittee.
implementation.responsibleParty: Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain; Gulf Coast Community Design Studio
implementation.sourceQuote: The first step in the planning process was to assemble a Watershed Implementation Team representing various stakeholders in Old Fort Bayou Watershed.

implementation.name: First Steering and Technical Advisory Committee meeting
implementation.description: The committee met to revisit the priorities and goals of the 2007 Action Plan. The resulting input was used to develop the vision and goals of the WIP.
implementation.responsibleParty: Steering and Technical Advisory Committee
implementation.sourceQuote: The Steering and Technical Advisory Committee first met on June 27, 2018 to revisit priorities and goals identified in the 2007 Action Plan based on current conditions.

implementation.name: Boat trip to document current conditions
implementation.description: Committee members took a day-long boat trip to explore and document conditions on Old Fort Bayou. This informed the watershed assessment and management plan.
implementation.responsibleParty: Steering and Technical Advisory Committee
implementation.sourceQuote: participated in a day-long boat trip to explore and document current conditions from the water on August 24, 2018.

implementation.name: Consultant analysis of water quality data against the TMDL
implementation.description: BMI Environmental Services and Nutter & Associates were hired to analyse available water quality data against the TMDL and thresholds. The work produced the fecal coliform TMDL reduction plan in Appendix D.
implementation.responsibleParty: BMI Environmental Services, LLC; Nutter & Associates
implementation.sourceQuote: BMI Environmental Services, LLC, in partnership with Nutter & Associates was hired as a project consultant between August and December 2018 to analyze available water quality data for Old Fort Bayou as compared to the TMDL and approved thresholds.

implementation.name: Final Watershed Advisory Team Meeting
implementation.description: The concluding planning meeting, where student work from the B-WET program was presented and incorporated into the plan.
implementation.responsibleParty: Watershed Advisory Team
implementation.sourceQuote: Student work was presented at the final Watershed Advisory Team Meeting on December 17, 2018

implementation.name: Education Subcommittee review of 2007 Action Plan strategies
implementation.description: The Education and Outreach Subcommittee reviewed the 2007 outreach strategies to determine their status. Those strategies informed the recommended activities in the WIP.
implementation.responsibleParty: Education and Outreach Subcommittee
implementation.sourceQuote: The Education and Outreach Subcommittee assembled as part of the development of this Watershed Implementation Plan revisited the strategies recommended in the Action Plan at a work session on August 27, 2018

implementation.name: Acquisition of 13.98 acres along Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla
implementation.description: The Land Trust is negotiating to acquire properties that would preserve riparian buffers and connect to land held by LTMCP and the St. Martin Schools.
implementation.responsibleParty: Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain
implementation.sourceQuote: The Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain is currently negotiating acquisition of several properties totaling 13.98 acres along Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla.

implementation.name: Restore St. Martin High School trail and outdoor classroom
implementation.description: LTMCP proposes working with students and Navy volunteers to restore an unused outdoor classroom and trail near Bayou Talla.
implementation.responsibleParty: Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain
implementation.sourceQuote: LTMCP has proposed working with students and a group of Navy Volunteers stationed in Pascagoula, MS to restore the trail and outdoor classroom.

implementation.name: Acquire property or easements to protect critical land
implementation.description: LTMCP should keep working with local jurisdictions and private landowners to acquire land or easements. The focus is on preserving, expanding and restoring riparian buffers along Old Fort Bayou.
implementation.responsibleParty: Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain; Jackson County; Ocean Springs; Gautier; private landowners
implementation.sourceQuote: LTMCP should continue to work with Jackson County, Ocean Springs, Gautier and private landowners within the watershed to acquire property or easements that will protect critical land within the watershed.

implementation.name: New kayak launch at The Inlets on Old Fort Bayou
implementation.description: LTMCP is building a new public kayak launch, expected to open in spring 2019, which will extend blueway infrastructure.
implementation.responsibleParty: Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain
implementation.sourceQuote: In addition, LTMCP is currently working on a new kayak launch adjacent to The Inlets development in Ocean Springs on Old Fort Bayou that is anticipated to be accessible to the public starting in the spring of 2019.

implementation.name: Blueway expansion up Bayou Talla and signage/print updates
implementation.description: Plans to extend the Old Fort Bayou blueway up Bayou Talla and to update printed material and signage are under way.
implementation.sourceQuote: Plans for an expansion up Bayou Talla and updates to both printed material and signage are in the works.

implementation.name: Student internship on stormwater barriers with Jackson County Planning
implementation.description: Through the B-WET program, four student interns will work with the Jackson County Planning Department to identify barriers to addressing stormwater and recommend solutions, including possible ordinance revisions.
implementation.responsibleParty: Gulf Coast Community Design Studio; Jackson County Planning Department; St. Martin High School students
implementation.sourceQuote: The program will continue through August 2019 and includes a summer internship for four students to work with the Jackson County Planning Department to identify barriers to addressing stormwater issues and recommend solutions.

implementation.name: Complete Mississippi-Louisiana golf course BMP manual
implementation.description: The joint MS-LA golf course BMP manual is expected to be completed in 2019. GCSAA is encouraging BMP implementation by 2020.
implementation.responsibleParty: Golf Course Superintendents Association of America; The Preserve Golf Club Director of Golf Operations
implementation.sourceQuote: Mississippi and Louisiana have made significant progress in developing their joint manual which should be completed in 2019. GCSAA is encouraging all manuals to be completed and BMPs to be implemented by 2020.

implementation.name: Refuge to develop a Visitor Services Plan
implementation.description: The plan recommends that the Mississippi Sandhill Crane National Wildlife Refuge make a Visitor Services Plan aligned with WIP goals a high priority.
implementation.responsibleParty: Mississippi Sandhill Crane National Wildlife Refuge
implementation.sourceQuote: Developing a Visitor Services Plan in line with the goals and objectives of the Old Fort Bayou Watershed Implementation Plan should be considered a high priority for the Refuge as a critical stakeholder in Old Fort Bayou Watershed.
implementation.sectionTitle: Promotion of Conservation Areas Open to the Public

implementation.name: Updated assessment of nonfunctioning septic systems
implementation.description: The 2008 septic survey should be updated to locate remaining nonfunctioning systems, paired with an education campaign on septic maintenance.
implementation.sourceQuote: An updated assessment of remaining nonfunctioning septic systems should be conducted, coupled with an educational campaign about the risks of nonfunctioning septic systems and proper maintenance.

implementation.name: Jackson County stormwater ordinance assessment
implementation.description: Assessment of stormwater, illicit discharge, flood damage and building code ordinances for Jackson County, to be completed through the B-WET program.
implementation.responsibleParty: Jackson County; St. Martin High School B-WET program
implementation.sourceQuote: This assessment is to be completed for Jackson County as part of the B-WET program underway with St. Martin High School as described above and in Appendix E.

implementation.name: MDEQ coastal supplement to stormwater technical manual
implementation.description: MDEQ should add a coastal supplement to its erosion and stormwater manual, or adopt Georgia's, and partner with other organisations to train jurisdictions and engineers.
implementation.responsibleParty: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality
implementation.sourceQuote: MDEQ should consider adding a coastal supplement to their technical manual so it is more relevant to jurisdictions on the coast or adopting Georgia’s Coastal Stormwater Supplement to the Georgia Stormwater Management Manual.

implementation.name: Increase capacity to monitor and enforce SWPPPs
implementation.description: Because active construction sites lack adequate controls, MDEQ and local jurisdictions should strengthen enforcement of construction stormwater pollution prevention plans.
implementation.responsibleParty: MDEQ and the jurisdictions
implementation.sourceQuote: MDEQ and the jurisdictions need to view erosion and stormwater control as a priority and increase their capacity to monitor and enforce SWPPP’s.

implementation.name: Jackson County to consider logging BMP ordinance
implementation.description: Recommendation that Jackson County adopt a timber harvest ordinance or similar mechanism to increase implementation of logging BMPs.
implementation.responsibleParty: Jackson County
implementation.sourceQuote: Jackson County should consider using a similar mechanism to increase the implementation of logging BMPs.

implementation.name: Assessment of remaining agricultural BMP opportunities
implementation.description: Conservation agencies assessed remaining BMP opportunities in the rural northern watershed. The result is the Table 4 list of recommended agricultural practices.
implementation.responsibleParty: Jackson County Soil and Water Conservation District; Mississippi Soil and Water Conservation Commission; USDA NRCS
implementation.timeframe: During the development of this Watershed Implementation Plan
implementation.sourceQuote: During the development of this Watershed Implementation Plan the Jackson County Soil and Water Conservation District in coordination with the Mississippi Soil and Water Conservation Commission and United States Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service assessed the remaining opportunities

monitoring.name: E. coli geometric mean criterion for Recreation
monitoring.description: The state bacteria standard for waters classified for Recreation, used to judge water quality in lower Old Fort Bayou: a geometric mean of 126 E. coli per 100 ml.
monitoring.unit: culturable e. coli bacteria per 100 ml
monitoring.location: Old Fort Bayou, Recreation classification (Biloxi Bay to Bayou Talla)
monitoring.sourceQuote: The current water quality standards for bacteria for Recreation set a threshold based on a geometric mean of 126 culturable e. coli bacteria per 100 ml
monitoring.sectionTitle: 2.4.4 Designated Use Classifications and Water Quality Standards

monitoring.name: E. coli single-sample criterion (410 per 100 ml)
monitoring.description: Samples analyzed during a 30-day period may not exceed 410 E. coli per 100 ml more than 10% of the time, under the Recreation standard applied to Old Fort Bayou.
monitoring.frequency: 30-day period; not more than 10% of the time
monitoring.sourceQuote: state that the samples analyzed during a 30-day period not exceed 410 e. coli per 100 ml more than 10% of the time
monitoring.sectionTitle: 2.4.4 Designated Use Classifications and Water Quality Standards

monitoring.name: Minimum bacteria sampling frequency
monitoring.description: The bacteria standard requires at least five samples over a 30-day period, with at least 12 hours between individual samples.
monitoring.frequency: Over a 30-day period, no less than 12 hours apart
monitoring.sourceQuote: there should be a minimum of five samples taken over a 30-day period with no less than 12 hours between individual samples
monitoring.sectionTitle: 2.4.4 Designated Use Classifications and Water Quality Standards

monitoring.name: MDEQ seasonal ambient monitoring at station #0481299
monitoring.description: MDEQ performs regular seasonal water quality monitoring at a state ambient station near the mouth of Old Fort Bayou. This is the main source of bacteria data for the plan.
monitoring.parameter: Fecal indicator bacteria (fecal coliform, E. coli)
monitoring.location: State ambient monitoring station #0481299 near the mouth of Old Fort Bayou
monitoring.sourceQuote: Seasonal water quality monitoring has been regularly performed by MDEQ at a state ambient monitoring station (#0481299) near the mouth of the Bayou in the area classified for Recreation.
monitoring.sectionTitle: 2.4.4 Designated Use Classifications and Water Quality Standards

monitoring.name: Proposed Total Nitrogen thresholds for southeast Mississippi streams
monitoring.description: Recommended TN thresholds of 0.31 to 0.68 mg/l, depending on the approach, to be considered if nutrient monitoring is arranged in the watershed.
monitoring.location: Southeast Mississippi rivers and streams (applied to Old Fort Bayou)
monitoring.sourceQuote: The recommended thresholds for TN in southeast Mississippi rivers and streams range from 0.31 to 0.68 mg/l, depending on the approach.
monitoring.sectionTitle: 2.4.4 Designated Use Classifications and Water Quality Standards

monitoring.name: Planned nutrient monitoring (TP and TN)
monitoring.description: Given current and future land use, the plan recommends also monitoring Total Phosphorus and Total Nitrogen.
monitoring.sourceQuote: it seems important to also monitor nutrients such as Total Phosphorus (TP) and Total Nitrogen (TN)
monitoring.sectionTitle: 2.4.4 Designated Use Classifications and Water Quality Standards

monitoring.name: Bacteria compliance status 2009-2017
monitoring.description: Baseline finding that, based on available bacterial data, Old Fort Bayou generally complied with the Recreation standards between 2009 and 2017.
monitoring.responsibleParty: BMI Environmental Services and Nutter & Associates (analysis)
monitoring.sourceQuote: Based on available bacterial data, it was determined that Old Fort Bayou was generally in compliance with MDEQ water quality standards for the Recreation classification between 2009 and 2017.

monitoring.name: Student water quality testing, spring 2019
monitoring.description: The B-WET student program will continue through August 2019, and another round of water quality testing is anticipated in spring 2019.
monitoring.parameter: Water temperature, turbidity, pH, dissolved oxygen, phosphorus, nitrates
monitoring.location: Two sites along Old Fort Bayou
monitoring.responsibleParty: St. Martin High School students / Gulf Coast Community Design Studio
monitoring.sourceQuote: The project will continue through August 2019 and it is anticipated that another round of water quality testing will be done in the spring of 2019.

monitoring.name: Water temperature - upstream (The Preserve Golf Club)
monitoring.description: Baseline water temperature measured by St. Martin High School students at the upstream site.
monitoring.location: The Preserve Golf Club, 901 MS-57, Vancleave (upstream)
monitoring.sourceQuote: Water Temperature | 20.1°C

monitoring.name: Water temperature - downstream (Twelve Oaks)
monitoring.description: Baseline water temperature measured by St. Martin High School students at the downstream site.
monitoring.location: Twelve Oaks, 1112 Hanley Rd, Ocean Springs (downstream)
monitoring.sourceQuote: Water Temperature | 23.2°C

monitoring.name: Turbidity - upstream (The Preserve Golf Club)
monitoring.description: Baseline turbidity measured by students at the upstream site, rated Good.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Turbidity | 30.6 JTU | Good

monitoring.name: Turbidity - downstream (Twelve Oaks)
monitoring.description: Baseline turbidity measured by students at the downstream site, rated Good.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Turbidity | 15.8 JTU | Good

monitoring.name: Dissolved oxygen - upstream (The Preserve Golf Club)
monitoring.description: Baseline dissolved oxygen saturation measured by students at the upstream site, rated Fair.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Dissolved Oxygen | 66% Saturation | Fair

monitoring.name: Dissolved oxygen - downstream (Twelve Oaks)
monitoring.description: Baseline dissolved oxygen saturation measured by students at the downstream site, rated Fair.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Dissolved Oxygen | 67% Saturation | Fair

monitoring.name: Phosphate - upstream (The Preserve Golf Club)
monitoring.description: Baseline phosphate concentration measured by students at the upstream site, rated Good.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Phosphate | 1.5 ppm | Good

monitoring.name: Phosphate - downstream (Twelve Oaks)
monitoring.description: Baseline phosphate concentration measured by students at the downstream site, rated Good. It is slightly higher than upstream.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Phosphate | 1.7 ppm | Good

monitoring.name: Nitrate - upstream (The Preserve Golf Club)
monitoring.description: Baseline nitrate concentration measured by students at the upstream site, rated Fair.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Nitrate | 5 ppm | Fair

monitoring.name: Nitrate - downstream (Twelve Oaks)
monitoring.description: Baseline nitrate concentration measured by students at the downstream site, rated Fair.
monitoring.sourceQuote: Nitrate | 5.1 ppm | Fair

monitoring.name: Student fecal coliform presence test
monitoring.description: Student kit tests for fecal coliform were positive at both sites. The plan notes this method is inaccurate and does not override MDEQ results.
monitoring.location: Two sites on Old Fort Bayou (The Preserve Golf Club and Twelve Oaks)
monitoring.sourceQuote: Tests at both sites showed positive results indicating higher levels of fecal coliform.

monitoring.name: 2017 Coastal Cleanup volunteers at Washington Avenue site
monitoring.description: Baseline participation in the 2017 Mississippi Coastal Cleanup at the watershed's only site: three volunteers covering less than a half mile.
monitoring.location: Washington Avenue boat launch, Ocean Springs
monitoring.sourceQuote: there were only three volunteers at that site and less than a half mile was covered. Six pounds of litter were reportedly collected

monitoring.name: 2017 litter collected at Washington Avenue site
monitoring.description: Baseline amount of litter collected in the 2017 Coastal Cleanup at the Old Fort Bayou site, mostly single-use plastics.
monitoring.location: Washington Avenue boat launch, Ocean Springs
monitoring.sourceQuote: Six pounds of litter were reportedly collected and of the litter collected, the majority was single-use plastics such as straws, bottles and bags.

monitoring.name: BMPs installed under 2001-2006 demonstration project
monitoring.description: Total number of BMPs installed by the Old Fort Bayou/Tuxachanie Creek Nonpoint Source Pollution Demonstration Project, covering 1,523 acres.
monitoring.location: Rural area of the Old Fort Bayou/Tuxachanie Creek watershed
monitoring.responsibleParty: Mississippi Soil and Water Conservation Commission and partners

monitoring.name: Soil saved by demonstration project BMPs
monitoring.description: Total tons of soil saved per year by the BMPs installed under the 2001-2006 demonstration project.
monitoring.parameter: Total Tons of Soil Saved Per Year
monitoring.location: Rural area of the Old Fort Bayou/Tuxachanie Creek watershed
monitoring.responsibleParty: Mississippi Soil and Water Conservation Commission and partners

monitoring.name: Expanded ambient monitoring at multiple sites
monitoring.description: The plan recommends continuing ambient water quality data collection at multiple sites throughout the watershed to better identify sources of impairment.
monitoring.location: Multiple sites throughout Old Fort Bayou Watershed
monitoring.sourceQuote: In general, ambient water quality data should continue to be collected, but from multiple sites throughout the watershed to give a more comprehensive picture of sources of impairments in Old Fort Bayou.

monitoring.name: Updated septic system survey
monitoring.description: The plan recommends updating the 2008 Mississippi Department of Health survey of septic systems in the watershed, coordinated with outreach to septic owners.
monitoring.sourceQuote: the most recent survey of septic systems in Old Fort Bayou Watershed was conducted by the Mississippi Department of Health in 2008. It would be beneficial to update the survey

monitoring.name: MDEQ post-BMP monitoring
monitoring.description: After BMP installation, MDEQ will monitor downstream water quality at locations chosen by best professional judgment, for comparison with pre-implementation data. This may require more than one year.
monitoring.frequency: After BMP installation; possibly more than 1 year
monitoring.sourceQuote: Post-BMP monitoring locations will be selected using best professional judgment and will be targeted to reflect water quality downstream of BMP activity.

monitoring.name: Restore Corps periodic monitoring
monitoring.description: If MDEQ cannot continue monitoring, the plan suggests partnering with the Gulf Coast Restore Corps for periodic water quality monitoring and visual assessments.
monitoring.parameter: Water quality and visual waterway assessments
monitoring.sourceQuote: If state agencies such as MDEQ are not able to continue monitoring in Old Fort Bayou in the future, consideration should be given to partnering with paid and semi-professional groups like the Gulf Coast Restore Corps for periodic monitoring and assessment.

monitoring.name: School water quality monitoring in Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla
monitoring.description: St. Martin High School is encouraged to continue monitoring water quality in Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla, with expansion to the middle and elementary schools.
monitoring.location: Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla
monitoring.sourceQuote: St. Martin High School is encouraged to keep monitoring water quality in Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla.

outreach.name: NOAA B-WET Old Fort Bayou Watershed Education program at St. Martin High School
outreach.description: A NOAA B-WET-funded watershed education program run by GCCDS with St. Martin High School students. Students tested water quality, learned about BMPs and contributed to the plan's vision and goals.
outreach.sourceQuote: the 80 students who participated in the NOAA Gulf of Mexico Bay Watershed Education and Training Program during the fall term at St. Martin High School

outreach.name: Student water quality monitoring field trip on Old Fort Bayou
outreach.description: Marine Science students monitored water quality at two sites on Old Fort Bayou with volunteers from partner agencies. Another round of testing is anticipated in spring 2019.
outreach.sourceQuote: GCCDS took students from the Marine Science classes at St. Martin High School to monitor water quality at two sites along Old Fort Bayou on Monday, December 5, 2018.

outreach.name: Summer internship for students with Jackson County Planning Department
outreach.description: Students will intern with the County Planning Department to identify barriers to addressing stormwater issues and to recommend Low Impact Development solutions.
outreach.sourceQuote: includes a summer internship for four students to work with the Jackson County Planning Department to identify barriers to addressing stormwater issues and recommend solutions

outreach.name: Steering and Technical Advisory Committee first meeting
outreach.description: A planning meeting held to revisit 2007 Action Plan priorities and to develop the vision and goals for the WIP.
outreach.sourceQuote: The Steering and Technical Advisory Committee first met on June 27, 2018 to revisit priorities and goals identified in the 2007 Action Plan based on current conditions.

outreach.name: Day-long boat trip to document bayou conditions
outreach.description: Committee members took a boat trip on Old Fort Bayou to explore and document current conditions from the water.
outreach.sourceQuote: participated in a day-long boat trip to explore and document current conditions from the water on August 24, 2018

outreach.name: Education and Outreach Subcommittee work session
outreach.description: A work session where the subcommittee reviewed the 2007 Action Plan outreach strategies and their status.
outreach.sourceQuote: The Education and Outreach Subcommittee assembled as part of the development of this Watershed Implementation Plan revisited the strategies recommended in the Action Plan at a work session on August 27, 2018

outreach.name: Third Steering and Technical Advisory Committee meeting at Gulf Hills
outreach.description: The third committee meeting, hosted by the manager of the Gulf Hills Hotel and Conference Center.
outreach.responsibleParty: Gulf Hills Hotel and Conference Center
outreach.sourceQuote: hosting the third meeting of the Steering and Technical Advisory Committee on September 25, 2018

outreach.name: Final Watershed Advisory Team Meeting with student presentations
outreach.description: The final planning meeting, at which St. Martin High School student work was presented.
outreach.sourceQuote: Student work was presented at the final Watershed Advisory Team Meeting on December 17, 2018

outreach.name: Expand school programming to St. Martin Middle and Elementary Schools
outreach.description: Continue the B-WET watershed programming and expand it to younger St. Martin students.
outreach.sourceQuote: Programming started with funding through the B-WET program at St. Martin High School should be continued and expanded to include St. Martin Middle and Elementary Schools.

outreach.name: Ocean Springs schools watershed programming
outreach.description: Ocean Springs schools near the bayou are recommended to include watershed and stormwater runoff programming specific to Old Fort Bayou.
outreach.sourceQuote: In addition, Ocean Springs’ schools should include programming focused on watershed dynamics and stormwater runoff specific to Old Fort Bayou Watershed.

outreach.name: Continued student water quality monitoring
outreach.description: St. Martin High School is encouraged to continue student monitoring of Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla, using supplies provided by the grant.
outreach.sourceQuote: St. Martin High School is encouraged to keep monitoring water quality in Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla.

outreach.name: Restore outdoor classroom and trail at St. Martin High School
outreach.description: LTMCP proposes working with students and Navy volunteers to restore an unused outdoor classroom and trail.
outreach.responsibleParty: Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain
outreach.sourceQuote: LTMCP has proposed working with students and a group of Navy Volunteers stationed in Pascagoula, MS to restore the trail and outdoor classroom.

outreach.name: Arts organizations outreach partnerships (WAMA, Mary C O'Keefe Cultural Center)
outreach.description: Partner with Ocean Springs arts organizations on watershed outreach with an art component and on demonstrations of small-scale urban BMPs.
outreach.sourceQuote: There are several arts organizations in Ocean Springs that would be excellent partners in terms of both demonstrating small-scale urban BMPs and watershed outreach and education with an art component.

outreach.name: Small-scale urban BMP demonstration projects
outreach.description: Highly visible demonstration projects such as rain gardens or rain barrels at businesses and organizations, paired with educational signage.
outreach.sourceQuote: In addition, small, highly-visible demonstration projects can be implemented at businesses and organizations in and around the watershed.

outreach.name: Low Impact Development education for jurisdictions and developers
outreach.description: Efforts to educate local jurisdictions on LID techniques and to give jurisdictions and developers tools to promote and use LID.
outreach.sourceQuote: Efforts are needed to educate the jurisdictions on Low Impact Development techniques and to provide the jurisdictions and developers with tools to increase their capacity to promote and use LID.

outreach.name: Training on stormwater technical manual
outreach.description: MDEQ is recommended to partner with Sea Grant, Grand Bay NERR or similar organizations to train jurisdictions and engineers on using the stormwater manual.
outreach.sourceQuote: MDEQ should look to partner with the Mississippi Alabama Sea Grant Consortium, Grand Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve (NERR), or similar organizations and agencies to provide training to jurisdictions and engineers on how to use the manual.

outreach.name: Old Fort Bayou watershed Facebook page
outreach.description: A Facebook page for watershed outreach, which could be maintained by the Jackson County Stormwater Task Force in place of a watershed partnership.
outreach.sourceQuote: In terms of watershed planning, a Facebook page is typically created and maintained by a watershed partnership.

outreach.name: Plastic Free Gulf Coast restaurant engagement
outreach.description: Encourage restaurants on Old Fort Bayou to join the Plastic Free Gulf Coast program to reduce single-use plastics and to educate residents.
outreach.responsibleParty: GCCDS; MSU Coastal Research and Extension Center
outreach.sourceQuote: In addition, there is an opportunity to work with restaurants in the watershed and particularly those on Old Fort Bayou to reduce the use of single-use plastics and educate residents.

outreach.name: Projects for Scout Troops
outreach.description: Volunteer projects for Boy and Girl Scouts tied to the Soil and Water Conservation Badge, plus a proposed fire ecology merit badge.
outreach.responsibleParty: Mississippi Sandhill Crane National Wildlife Refuge
outreach.sourceQuote: Appendix I includes sample projects for Boy Scouts related to the Soil and Water Conservation Badge. The Mississippi Sandhill Crane National Wildlife Refuge also recommends developing a fire ecology merit badge.

outreach.name: Septic system maintenance educational campaign
outreach.description: A campaign on the risks of nonfunctioning septic systems and proper maintenance, targeted at areas with many remaining septic systems.
outreach.sourceQuote: an educational campaign about the risks of nonfunctioning septic system and proper maintenance should target areas in the watershed where high concentrations of septic systems remain.

outreach.name: Educational signage at public BMPs, access points and trails
outreach.description: Educational signage to be installed alongside publicly accessible BMPs and at public access points and trails.
outreach.sourceQuote: Educational signage should be installed when publically accessible BMPs are installed. If not already present, signage should be added at public access point or trails.

outreach.name: Old Fort Bayou Watershed signs
outreach.description: General watershed signs placed strategically around the watershed as a low-cost way to raise awareness.
outreach.sourceQuote: It is also recommended that general Old Fort Bayou Watershed Signs be added strategically throughout the watershed.

outreach.name: Blueway expansion and signage/printed material updates
outreach.description: Planned updates to blueway printed material and signage, including expansion up Bayou Talla.
outreach.responsibleParty: Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain
outreach.sourceQuote: Plans for an expansion up Bayou Talla and updates to both printed material and signage are in the works.

outreach.name: Print updated Old Fort Bayou Blueway brochure
outreach.description: LTMCP has funding to print the 2018 updated blueway brochure, which will also need to include new blueway infrastructure.
outreach.responsibleParty: Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain
outreach.sourceQuote: LTMCP currently has funding to print the updated brochure.

outreach.name: No wake zone education signage
outreach.description: Signage or other public education on scouring caused by boat wake.
outreach.sourceQuote: Signage or other means of educating the public on water quality impairments caused by scouring associated with wave action may be necessary.

outreach.name: Pet waste disposal education
outreach.description: Education on proper pet waste disposal, distributed by local jurisdictions, property owners associations and pet-related businesses.
outreach.responsibleParty: local jurisdictions, property owners associations, pet-related businesses
outreach.sourceQuote: Education around proper disposal of pet waste should be distributed by the local jurisdictions, property owners associations, and local pet-related businesses such as

outreach.name: Pet waste signage and receptacles
outreach.description: Signage and waste receptacles in areas where people frequently walk pets.
outreach.sourceQuote: Signage and waste receptacles should also be provided in areas where people frequently walk pets.

outreach.name: Promote use of native plants
outreach.description: Garden clubs and nurseries are proposed to promote native plants to residents in place of grass or invasive species.
outreach.sourceQuote: Local garden clubs and nurseries would be ideal promoters of the use of native plants.

outreach.name: Responsible fertilizer use outreach
outreach.description: Outreach to property owners and lawn care businesses on responsible fertilizer use, coordinated with a possible fertilizer ordinance.
outreach.audience: property owners and lawn care businesses
outreach.responsibleParty: jurisdictions in Old Fort Bayou Watershed
outreach.sourceQuote: in coordination with education and outreach to property owners and lawn care businesses about responsible fertilizer use

outreach.name: Mississippi Coastal Cleanup extension
outreach.description: Increase volunteers at the Old Fort Bayou cleanup site, add upstream sites and add cleanup from the water.
outreach.sourceQuote: Additional efforts to increase the number of volunteers is recommended, in addition to adding a cleanup site or sites further upstream.

outreach.name: Illegal dumping awareness
outreach.description: Efforts to make residents aware of proper disposal options and the consequences of illegal dumping.
outreach.sourceQuote: additional efforts may need to focus on making residents aware of their options for proper disposal and/or the consequences of illegal dumping.

outreach.name: Demonstration project education (farms, field days, press releases, fact sheets)
outreach.description: Education and outreach reported for the 2001-2006 Old Fort Bayou/Tuxachanie Creek demonstration project.
outreach.responsibleParty: Mississippi Soil and Water Conservation Commission and partners
outreach.sourceQuote: Education and outreach included demonstration farms, educational field days, press releases and fact sheets.

geographicAreas.name: Old Fort Bayou Watershed
geographicAreas.description: The 32,082-acre watershed the plan covers, identified by HUC 031700090604. It spans parts of Ocean Springs, Gautier and Jackson County.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The Old Fort Bayou Watershed (HUC 031700090604) is 32,082 acres and includes parts of the City of Ocean Springs, the City of Gautier and Jackson County.
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: 1.1.2 Why create a WIP for Old Fort Bayou?

geographicAreas.name: Old Fort Bayou (Waterbody ID MS118M1)
geographicAreas.description: The main tidal waterbody of the watershed. It was listed on the 1998 303(d) list for fecal coliform and is the subject of the TMDL.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Old Fort Bayou (Waterbody ID MS118M1) is a tributary of the Back Bay of Biloxi and Biloxi Bay
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: 1.1.2 Why create a WIP for Old Fort Bayou?

geographicAreas.name: Back Bay of Biloxi and Biloxi Bay
geographicAreas.description: The receiving waters of Old Fort Bayou. The 2002 fecal coliform TMDL the plan addresses was written for them.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Old Fort Bayou (Waterbody ID MS118M1) is a tributary of the Back Bay of Biloxi and Biloxi Bay
geographicAreas.sectionTitle: 1.1.2 Why create a WIP for Old Fort Bayou?

geographicAreas.name: Bayou Talla
geographicAreas.description: A significant offshoot of Old Fort Bayou next to the St. Martin Schools. It is proposed for blueway extension, conservation and monitoring.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Bayou Talla is a significant offshoot of Old Fort Bayou that is adjacent to the St. Martin Schools that are part of the Jackson Country School District.

geographicAreas.name: City of Ocean Springs
geographicAreas.description: A municipality covering the southwest part of the watershed.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The watershed includes part of the City of Ocean Springs to the southwest, part of Gautier to the southeast, and spans into Jackson County to the north.

geographicAreas.name: City of Gautier
geographicAreas.description: A municipality covering the southeast part of the watershed.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The watershed includes part of the City of Ocean Springs to the southwest, part of Gautier to the southeast, and spans into Jackson County to the north.

geographicAreas.name: Jackson County
geographicAreas.description: The county the watershed lies in. It covers the northern, unincorporated part of the watershed.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The watershed includes part of the City of Ocean Springs to the southwest, part of Gautier to the southeast, and spans into Jackson County to the north.

geographicAreas.name: St. Martin community
geographicAreas.description: An unincorporated community bordering the lower watershed to the north, where considerable development is occurring.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The lower watershed is bordered by the St. Martin community to the north and the City of Ocean Springs to the south.

geographicAreas.name: Northern subunit
geographicAreas.description: The rural northern subunit of the watershed, defined in the 2018 analysis. Livestock runoff and failing septic systems are the likely pathogen sources here.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The northern unit is more rural and has some agricultural uses and low-intensity development.

geographicAreas.name: Middle subunit
geographicAreas.description: The middle subunit of the watershed, made up mainly of conservation lands. Pathogen sources here are likely wildlife or limited development.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The middle unit consists mainly of conservation lands.

geographicAreas.name: Lower (southern) subunit
geographicAreas.description: The more intensely developed southern subunit. Stormwater runoff, sewer overflows and direct deposits are the likely main pathogen sources.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The lower unit has higher intensity development and developing areas.

geographicAreas.name: Mississippi Sandhill Crane National Wildlife Refuge
geographicAreas.description: A federal refuge of about 19,300 acres in three units. It is a major stakeholder and conservation landholder in the watershed.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The Mississippi Sandhill Crane Refuge consists of three separate units totaling approximately 19,300 acres: the Gautier, Ocean Springs, and Fontainebleau units.

geographicAreas.name: Bayou Talla conservation and restoration properties
geographicAreas.description: A priority project area along Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla, totaling 13.98 acres, that LTMCP is negotiating to acquire to protect riparian buffers.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The Land Trust for the Mississippi Coastal Plain is currently negotiating acquisition of several properties totaling 13.98 acres along Old Fort Bayou and Bayou Talla.

geographicAreas.name: Old Fort Bayou Mitigation Bank (TNC)
geographicAreas.description: The Nature Conservancy's nature preserve and mitigation bank in the watershed, where wet pine savanna restoration BMPs are carried out.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: TNC implements a number of BMPs focused on wet pine savanna restoration on their Old Fort Bayou Mitigation Bank.

geographicAreas.name: The Preserve Golf Club
geographicAreas.description: A golf course next to Old Fort Bayou in Vancleave. It showcases golf course BMPs and is a priority site in the plan.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The Preserve Golf Club, located in Vancleave and adjacent to Old Fort Bayou, has been a certified Audubon Signature Sanctuary since 2007.

geographicAreas.name: Gulf Hills Golf Course
geographicAreas.description: A golf course just outside the watershed boundary that drains into Old Fort Bayou. It is included in the plan's golf course BMP recommendations.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: Further downstream on Old Fort Bayou is Gulf Hills Golf Course.

geographicAreas.name: Old Fort Bayou/Tuxachanie Creek Watershed demonstration project area
geographicAreas.description: The 102,000-acre watershed where the 2001-2006 nonpoint source demonstration project installed agricultural BMPs.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The project began in November 2001 and concluded in September 2006 and resulted in the installation of a significant number of BMPs within the rural area of the 102,000-acre watershed
